findings.title: Organization slug logic inverted (unrelated change)
findings.body: The condition was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts the behaviour: the team's `slug` is now only persisted when team billing *is* enabled, and in that case both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` are set simultaneously. On self-hosted/billing-disabled instances the organization is now created with `slug = null`, so its subdomain/org lookup (`orgDomains`, `slugCollisions` checks, org URLs) will not resolve. This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor and should be reverted or corrected to `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`.

findings.title: TypeError when location is Google Meet and no destination calendar exists
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null, and line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. For any booking whose location is Google Meet and whose organizer/event type has no destination calendar (previously handled safely via `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), `EventManager.create()` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, failing the whole booking instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: credentialId is no longer stored for video booking references
findings.body: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the credentialId for non-calendar (video) results; the previous code stored `result.credentialId` for video results. Cancellation logic in `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (`if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`), so video meetings created after this change will never be deleted on cancellation, and other code paths that resolve a video credential from the reference will also break.

findings.title: Destination-calendar fallback in updateEvent/deleteEvent can never match
findings.body: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares each `externalId` against `undefined`/`null` and always returns `undefined`. The pre-change fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Consequence: when a booking reference has no `externalCalendarId`, `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined` (request fails / wrong target) instead of the configured destination calendar. The same broken predicate is used at line 317 in `deleteEvent`, where it silently falls back to `primary` and the event in the destination calendar is never deleted.

findings.title: createEvent falls back to "primary" when destination calendar has no credentialId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now resolved only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. Destination calendars stored without a `credentialId` (legacy rows, and the event-type destination calendar path in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` which calls `createEvent(c, event)` without an externalId) will not match, so the event is created in the account's `primary` calendar instead of the user-selected destination calendar. Previously `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId` was used unconditionally. Consider keeping an `externalId` fallback when no credentialId match is found.

findings.title: events.patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId
findings.body: The insert call guards with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (used to write the hangout link into the description) passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When `selectedCalendar` is undefined (no destination calendar matching the credentialId), the event is created in `primary` but the patch request targets an undefined calendar and fails, so Google Meet links are missing from the calendar event description.

findings.title: Team destination calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and the collective branch then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Because of the optional chaining the collected host calendars are silently discarded in exactly the case the PR aims to fix (organizer without a destination calendar, other collective hosts with one). Initialize the array (e.g. `[]`) and push, or build the array from all sources before assigning.

findings.title: updateLocation no longer records externalCalendarId on references
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` in `updateLocation` now uses `result.externalId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never sets `externalId` on its `EventResult` (only `createEvent` does). Previously the value came from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. As a result, booking references recreated after a location change get `externalCalendarId: undefined`, so later updates/cancellations can no longer target the correct external calendar (see the Google `deleteEvent`/`updateEvent` fallbacks, which require it).

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes every event once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring-event branch (iterating all of the user's calendar credentials × all `updatedBookings` × each booking's first calendar reference) is now executed inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references the same delete requests are issued N times, multiplying external API calls and producing repeated 404/410 responses. The recurring branch should be hoisted out of the per-reference loop (or keyed on the current reference) instead of re-running for each one.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents error is no longer logged
findings.body: The `catch` block still builds the diagnostic `message` string (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed, so `message` is now dead code and calendar-update failures are swallowed with no trace in the logs. Either log the message or remove it.

findings.title: updateEvent may be called with an undefined credential
findings.body: Inside the `reference.credentialId` branch, if neither `this.calendarCredentials` nor the DB lookup yields a credential (e.g. credential deleted, or app slug missing), `credential` stays `undefined` and `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is still invoked, which will throw when it dereferences `credential.appName`/`credential.type`. Guard with `if (credential)` and push a failed `EventResult` otherwise so the booking flow reports the app status instead of hitting the generic catch.

findings.title: organization.slug removed from dynamic-booking user select
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` for dynamic (no eventTypeId) bookings no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, which the previous query included. Any downstream consumer of the organizer's `organization.slug` (org-aware booker/webapp URLs) will now see `undefined` for dynamic group bookings. This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor; restore the field unless it is provably unused.

findings.title: Invalid dynamicUserList surfaces as 500 instead of 400
findings.body: `throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is caught by the new try/catch, which only maps `HttpError` and `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to a 400; a plain `Error` falls through to `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. A malformed client request therefore reports a server error and the real reason is lost. Throw `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })` directly for this validation.

findings.title: Webhook payload shape for destinationCalendar is now inconsistent (null vs [] vs array)
findings.body: `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` changed from an object to an array, which is a breaking change for webhook/API consumers. The payload is now inconsistent across triggers: BOOKING_REJECTED expects `[]` (confirm.handler returns `[]`), while BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect `null` (handleNewBooking assigns `null` when no calendar is found). Normalize to a single representation (always an array) and document the breaking payload change.

findings.title: No tests for multi-destination-calendar creation/update paths
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents` and `updateAllCalendarEvents` were substantially rewritten (loops over multiple destination calendars, per-reference credential resolution, DB credential fallback), and `EventResult.externalId`/`credentialId` now drive `referencesToCreate`. There are no unit tests covering: multiple destination calendars producing one reference per calendar with the correct `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId`, the empty destinationCalendar fallback, and the video-reference credentialId. Given the regressions these fields cause in cancel/reschedule flows, tests here would prevent silent breakage.
